title: Private deployment marketplace compatibility and tenant onboarding guide
content:
Purpose
This doc is a pragmatic preflight + onboarding playbook for partners that want to list Redwood Inference offerings which include a private-deploy option (VPC / on-prem) on cloud marketplaces and partner portals. It focuses on technical compatibility, procurement/entitlement mapping, and the tenant onboarding cadence we recommend so PM/AE/partner teams can run launches with fewer back-and-forths.

Audience
- Marketplace PMs and partner-engineering leads
- Solutions engineers who will enable private tenant installs
- Legal/Procurement stakeholders responsible for entitlements and SLAs

High-level problem we solve
Many marketplace listings are written and tested against hosted SaaS flows. Private deployments introduce extra friction: network setup (VPC peering, private link), KMS/HSM key access, compliance checks, regional SKU mapping, and a different entitlements/provisioning path. This guide standardizes requirements and provides copy templates and a step-by-step onboarding cadence to reduce cycle time.

Preflight checklist (technical compatibility)
- Supported topology: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Endpoint, GCP Private Service Connect documented? (yes/no)
- Minimum infra footprint: recommended GPU types, baseline CPU/RAM for control-plane agent, disk IO profile
- KMS/HSM integration options: customer-managed keys supported and tested (Y/N) + sample key policy
- Network egress exceptions: outbound IP ranges, required CIDR blocks, and DNS records to allow control-plane connectivity
- Audit logs forwarding: supported sinks (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Azure Monitor / syslog) and sample collector config
- Authentication: SSO options supported (SAML/OIDC), service principal flow, short-lived certs, and token refresh lifecycle
- Entitlement enforcement: SKU mapping to tenant license + trial grace behavior (e.g., 14 days trial then require activation)
- Data residency: region pinning supported (yes/no) and any limitations with private deployments
- Upgrade strategy: in-place upgrades vs. blue/green for private installs, expected downtime windows
- Telemetry & observability: required agent metrics, trace endpoints, and minimum retention expectations for support debugging
- Backoff/fallback policies: how runtime falls back to hosted model variants if local capacity exhausted (opt-in only)

Procurement & entitlement mapping checklist
- Marketplace SKU model: define distinct SKUs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (example: RI-API-HOSTED, RI-DEDICATED-M, RI-PRIVATE-PER-TENANT)
- Trial provisioning path: one-click trial for hosted; private trials require a provisioning ticket with partner SE and automatic 14-day trial SKU mapping
- Metering vs. seat: clearly call out metered usage (tokens/embeddings) vs. fixed-seat or reserved capacity entitlements for private deployments
- Invoice & billing hooks: what metadata the marketplace needs to send back to Redwood (customer id, tenant id, sku id)
- SKUs per region: recommended mapping for EMEA/APAC (note any legal/regulatory holdouts e.g., China)

Security & compliance gating
- Minimum security review checklist for private installs: network diagram, KMS policy, admin user list, retention policy for logs
- SLA attachment: what can be guaranteed in a private deployment and what remains best-effort (call out that Dedicated SLA language should be used when reserved capacity is purchased)
- Audit package: template of artifacts we require for listing (SOC2 section, dataflow diagrams, encryption-at-rest details)
- PII redaction guidance: recommended default settings for telemetry and prompt logging for regulated customers

Onboarding cadence (4–6 week recommended playbook)
Week 0: Intake and validation\- Partner/Customer fills marketplace provisioning form (auto creates a ticket in JIRA with links to marketplace order)\- SE validates entitlement and selects appropriate SKU and trial options
Week 1: Network & infra readiness\- Confirm VPC connectivity option; exchange CIDR/VPN details; validate outbound allowlists\- If KMS/HSM used, exchange IAM policy snippet and perform test key-wrap handshake
Week 2: Deployment & smoke test\- Deploy control-plane agent and inference nodes; run smoke tests (latency SLO check, model load, simple generate endpoints)\- Verify audit log forwarding and metrics ingestion to our TS/observability workspace
Week 3: Performance tuning and cost controls\- Suggest batching/quantization profile for production workload\- Recommend cache TTLs and autoscaling thresholds for cost predictability
Week 4: Cutover & handoff\- Conduct runbook walkthrough with customer ops; confirm support escalation path and monitoring dashboards\- Create final acceptance ticket in marketplace portal to move from trial to paid SKU
Optional Week 5–6: Post-launch optimization\- Run a 2-week observation window for regressions and recommend Optimize settings (quantization, batch sizes)

Marketplace tile copy (short + long variants)
Short title (15–30 chars): "Redwood Inference — Private Deploy"
Short blurb (1 line): "High-performance LLM inference in your VPC or on-prem, with enterprise controls and SLA options."
Long blurb (3–4 lines): "Run Redwood Inference behind your network boundary for full data control. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments with KMS support, audit logging, and predictable throughput. Fast setup for trials with partner-assisted provisioning and clear upgrade paths for production."
Bullets for asset panel (3–5 bullets):
- GPU-optimized runtime with batching, KV-caching, and quantized execution
- VPC / PrivateLink / Private Endpoint deployment options
- Customer-managed keys, audit logs, and regional residency options
- Dedicated SLA and reserved capacity available
CTA suggestions:
- Primary CTA: "Start private trial"
- Secondary CTA: "Talk to sales"

Customer-facing copy variants for sales/AE use (short email snippets)
- Variant A (technical): "We can provision a 14-day private trial in your VPC. Our SE will validate your network and KMS settings, deploy a control-plane agent, and run a smoke test — typically < 7 business days to the first inference result."
- Variant B (procurement): "This listing supports marketplace invoicing and regional SKUs. Select the private deployment SKU and we’ll handle license activation and a partner-assisted trial."

Telemetry & support expectations (what partner should provide)
- Required: access to metrics endpoint or a read-only role to view observability (dashboards), one-week logs with request ids for debugging\- Recommended: a pre-defined sample workload and latency SLO target so we can tune batching/cache profiles\- Support handoff: SE escalation contact, on-call rotation for first 30 days, and postmortem cadence for significant incidents

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Network blackholing: validate outbound allowlists early; provide a small connectivity test script for partners to run\- KMS policy blocks: share policy snippet and a test-key exchange step in Week 1\- Overloaded tenant nodes: default autoscaling thresholds tend to be conservative — recommend a tuning plan and an optional reserved-capacity SKU for production

Operational runbooks (quick snippets to include with marketplace assets)
- Rollback criteria: if > 5% error rate on inference over 15 minutes or latency > 3x target for > 10 minutes, rollback to previous bundle and notify SE\- Emergency fallback: opt-in policy to allow runtime to route to hosted variant (explicit customer consent required)

Things legal/procurement will ask (prep answers)
- Do we accept marketplace invoicing? Yes, but invoice metadata must include tenant id (sample payload attached in Confluence)
- Who owns keys? Customer owns KMS keys; Redwood needs a short-lived key-wrap token to perform image encryption during installs if requested
- Can we provide audit logs for compliance? Yes — forward to customer sink; retention policy configurable per contract

Open questions and decisions needed
- Do we list a single SKU per cloud with a regional flag, or create explicit regional SKUs (pricing/procurement complexity vs. legal clarity)?
- Default trial length for private installs (14 days recommended). Confirm with legal if an extended trial requires a written MSA addendum.
- Fallback routing policy opt-in: do we default to disabled or enabled with explicit checkbox on provisioning form?

Appendix: sample marketplace tile copy (ready-to-send)
Title: "Redwood Inference — Private Deployment"
One-liner: "Bring high-throughput LLM inference into your VPC or datacenter with enterprise controls, KMS support, and reserved capacity options."
3 bullets:
1) "Low-latency inference: GPU-optimized runtime + smart batching to reduce cost and latency"
2) "Data controls: Customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and region pinning"
3) "Flexible economics: hosted API, dedicated pools, or private tenant installs — pick what fits your compliance and budget needs"
CTA: "Request private trial"

Next steps (owner: Diego Morales)
- Review with Legal (Janelle) by 2025-11-21
- Finalize SKU mapping with Finance (Samir) by 2025-11-25
- Run a pilot listing in the AWS Marketplace sandbox with Partner Eng by 2025-12-05

Notes to self (working)
- Keep copy succinct and avoid implying we support all on-prem topologies — be explicit about what we test\- Add a small connectivity checker repo link to the marketplace assets so customers can self-validate before provisioning

End of doc
